question: The B-2-2 Tourist/Transit (Jeju) guide says foreigners can enter Jeju without a visa. How long can they stay, where may they go, how must they arrive, and does anything else in the corpus change this?
reference: The guide allows a stay of 30 days, limited to Jeju, and requires arriving by a direct international flight or ship to Jeju; citizens of the listed restricted countries are excluded. However, a notice that took effect on February 4, 2020 temporarily suspended visa-free entry to Jeju for all foreign nationals.
answer: Foreigners can enter Jeju without a visa unless they are citizens of 24 countries that require visas to enter Jeju island [1]. The duration of stay depends on the type of transfer passenger: General Transfer Passengers may stay for up to 72 hours, while Jeju Group Transfer Passengers may stay for up to 15 days (or 10 days if entering through Yangyang Airport) [1]. General Transfer Passengers must possess a transfer ticket and stay in the Seoul Capital Area, whereas Jeju Group Transfer Passengers must have a domestic flight/ship ticket to Jeju scheduled to depart within 5 days (or 10 days for Yangyang entrants) [1]. Eligible applicants for visa-free entry include foreign nationals entering ports and airports in Jeju for tourism/transit, as well as specific transfer passengers meeting the conditions above [1]. The list of countries requiring visas to enter Jeju includes Syria, Sudan, Iran, Macedonia, Cuba, Republic Of Kosovo, Palestine, Afghanistan, Iraq, Nigeria, Ghana, Yemen, Gambia, Senegal, Bangladesh, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Somalia, Uzbekistan, Nepal, Cameroon, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Egypt [1]. Even if a foreigner has a valid visa or is subject to visa-free entry, they may be denied entry if found inadmissible by an immigration officer at the port of entry [1].

cited_passages.title: Visa guide: B-2-2 Tourist / Transit (Jeju)

They will receive a multiple-entry visa valid for 5 years with a period of stay granted for up to 90 days [1].
